links.outcome: Alarm burden and sensitivity/PPV under different alarm policies in simulated real-time use
links.effect: With a 24 h expected alarm window and multi-threshold alarm policy: sensitivity 71.6%, PPV 9.9%, average 1.15 alarms per day per patient.
links.quote: When setting the expected alarm window to 24 h and using a multi-threshold alarm policy, the sensitivity metric was 71.6 %, while the positive predictive value was 9.9 %, resulting in an average of 1.15 alarms per day per patient.

links.effect: Best feature model AUC six hours before CRASH was 0.875 (0.072), versus other six models 0.782 (0.089) to 0.846 (0.083).
links.quote: When tested by seven-fold cross-validations, the mean (standard deviation) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) six hours before CRASH was 0.875 (0.072) for the best performing model, compared to the other six models with AUC ranging from 0.782 (0.089) to 0.846 (0.083).
